title: Karabakh Armenian forces accept a ceasefire and agree to disarm after one day of fighting
body:
A ceasefire between Azerbaijan and ethnic Armenian forces in Nagorno-Karabakh took effect at 1 pm local time on Wednesday, 20 September 2023, a day after Azerbaijan began its offensive. The ethnic Armenian forces accepted a Russian proposal, and Azerbaijan's Ministry of Defence confirmed the agreement. Russia's Ministry of Defence said the ceasefire would be implemented with the Russian peacekeepers stationed in the region. According to the Russian news agency Interfax, remaining Armenian army units would withdraw from Nagorno-Karabakh and Karabakh fighters would surrender their weapons.

The Azerbaijani presidential office confirmed that talks with Armenian separatists on reintegration would be held in Yevlakh on Thursday. Azerbaijan's foreign ministry spokesperson Aykhan Hajizada said peace would come after Armenian forces disarmed and withdrew and the regime was disbanded. Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said Armenia had not helped draft the deal and that Armenia had no army in Nagorno-Karabakh. Moscow said 2,261 people, including 1,049 children, were sheltering at the peacekeepers' base camp.

Al Jazeera reported that dozens of people were killed, without attributing a figure, and noted visible damage in the regional capital Stepanakert. The Kremlin rejected criticism of its handling of the crisis, and President Vladimir Putin said the peacekeepers would protect the civilian population. Pashinyan faced calls to resign, and Armenia's security council warned of large-scale unrest after protests on 19 September.
